# Case-study brief and source

SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.

## Brief

Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.

## Material

Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.

The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.

Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:

- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.

## Forbidden inferences / judging

No claim that software caused the shorter assignment time, saved money, delighted residents or rescued a helpless customer. Do not turn assignment time into completion time. The customer's reservation must survive. Judge whether quotations contribute experience beyond the surrounding narrative, whether supplier narration stays in third person and whether the suggested link accurately describes its destination.
# Elm Quay samlar reparationsanmälningar i en gemensam vy

Ett åtta veckor långt försök i två byggnader gav Elm Quay Housing underlag för att bedöma en gemensam reparationslogg. Här beskriver underhållsteamet sina val, arbetet med kategorierna och vad mätningen kan säga. Kundfallet publiceras av leverantören Svale Systems.

Av [ditt namn]

Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter. Tidigare förvarades telefonanmälningar och mejl separat. I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att prova en gemensam reparationslogg i två byggnader. Målet var att personal på olika skift skulle kunna se samma information.

## Elm Quay behöll telefonanmälningarna

Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör. De boende kunde fortsätta att anmäla reparationer per telefon, medan Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen.

Arbetsledaren för underhåll, Maya Lind, beskriver i en mejlintervju vad teamet ville åstadkomma:

– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle kunna se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.

## Försöket omfattade 31 reparationsanmälningar

Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, redovisar tiden från anmälan till tilldelning. Medianen var två arbetsdagar under försöket, jämfört med tre under den föregående åttaveckorsperioden. Akuta ärenden och arbeten beställda före försöket ingår inte i anteckningens underlag.

Perioderna hade olika arbetsbelastning. Anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden i tid. Det finns heller inga mätningar av kostnader, boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var slutförda. Siffrorna ger därför inget besked om besparingar eller snabbare slutförda arbeten.

## Teamets beslut om fler byggnader återstår

Försöket har ännu inte utökats. Teamet ska besluta efter att ha kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer. När Maya Lind ser tillbaka på förberedelserna beskriver arbetsledaren en erfarenhet inför nästa byggnad:

– Vi ägnade mer tid åt att enas om kategorierna än åt att lägga in de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar.

– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. Att ha en gemensam vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser, säger Maya Lind om försöket.

## Läs checklistan inför genomförandet

Elm Quays erfarenhet visar vilka val och begränsningar ett försök kan behöva belysa. För dig som vill läsa vidare finns [Svales checklista för genomförandet](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).
Resolved language: sv (Swedish). Source quotation language: English. Target quotation language: Swedish.

## Claims

Every claim is supported by the text or its material, with exact attribution and proportionate strength. Preserve the state of knowledge: what is unknown or unclaimed is not thereby known not to have happened. Keep uncertainty where it exists and certainty where it is warranted. A fact, quotation, source, scene, personal experience or opinion attributed to somebody is never invented to complete a form. Name the actual source of an attributed claim rather than invoking unnamed studies or experts.

Circumstantial detail is a claim too: duration, manner, motive, absence and background all need support. So does an evaluative characterisation: calling a count high, low or modest needs a comparison, target, capacity or speaker assessment. Otherwise give the count with its exclusions, without that assessment.

A sequence or correlation establishes no cause. A causal verb such as *shortened* needs causal support; a causal hedge such as *suggests that it shortened* still adds that attribution. This boundary holds in the title, summary, headings and body alike. Preserve chronology, scope and qualifications wherever a claim appears.

A stated length constrains the use of material and is never a licence to add to it. When the material is insufficient, deliver the length the material supports and name what further material would close the gap. A supplied publication limit is binding; meeting it cannot justify invention or loss of a qualification that changes a claim.

# Quoting speech

Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.

Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.

When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.

## What may be repaired

The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

## What stays outside this

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.

## Swedish composition
Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

## Source-support findings

### S1 — Entered-report count becomes the scope of the trial

Draft: “Försöket omfattade 31 reparationsanmälningar”.

Source: “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”

Change: the thing counted and its scope. The source counts entered reports in an explicitly restricted record; the heading ordinarily supplies the number of reports encompassed by the trial. The body provides exclusions but never supplies the source's verb “entered”.

Countercase, source true / draft false: 31 ordinary reports were entered, while a further report handled in the trial was not entered, or an emergency report was outside the note's count. The trial encompassed more than 31 reports. Nothing supplied says that every trial report was entered or that excluded work lay wholly outside the trial's activity.

Reverse, draft true / source false: the trial encompasses 31 reports in total but only 30 are entered. This demonstrates that total trial scope alone does not establish the source's recorded-count proposition; the actual supplied count rules that hypothetical source-false situation out, but does not make the two propositions equivalent.

Smallest supported repair: “31 reparationsanmälningar registrerades under försöket”. Retain the body's exclusions and exact attribution to the internal note.

### S2 — “Emergencies” broadens to acute/urgent cases

Draft: “Akuta ärenden ... ingår inte i anteckningens underlag.”

Source: “It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”

Change: named exclusion category. “Akuta ärenden” can include urgent repair cases that are not emergencies. The package supplies no shared definition that makes every acute/urgent case an emergency.

Countercase, source true / draft false: a repair requires prompt attention because a temporarily unusable shared facility is urgently needed, but there is no emergency. The note includes that urgent case while excluding emergencies. The Swedish exclusion can deny its inclusion. No supplied sentence excludes inclusion of urgent non-emergency cases.

Reverse, draft true / source false: exclusion of all urgent cases could coexist with inclusion of a report documenting an already resolved emergency, classified as nonurgent at reporting. Whether the source's “emergencies” category follows the event or current priority is unspecified; thus “akuta ärenden” cannot establish the exact source exclusion either. The actual source explicitly excludes emergencies, but supplies no criterion equating this with Swedish urgency classification.

Smallest supported repair: “Anmälningar som gäller nödsituationer och arbeten beställda före försöket ingår inte i anteckningens underlag.” This keeps the restricted record and pretrial-work exclusion, while naming the emergency category.

### S3 — The pending expansion decision is narrowed to more buildings

Draft: “Teamets beslut om fler byggnader återstår”.

Source: “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.” The quotation supplies “I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

Change: subject/scope of the pending decision. The source factual statement concerns expansion generally. The quotation is the supervisor's conditional preparation advice; it does not make a pending team decision about additional buildings a fact.

Countercase, source true / draft false: the team will decide whether to expand the range of repairs handled in the same two buildings, after checking larger repairs. It has no pending decision on further buildings. Lind can still offer advice for any eventual next building. No source sentence requires geographical expansion as the immediate decision.

Reverse, draft true / source false: a decision about further buildings is pending, while expansion within the original buildings has already occurred, or the decision is to be taken without the specified category check. A buildings-decision heading alone does not carry the source's unexpanded status and prerequisite. The source's explicit unexpanded status and prerequisite exclude these as actual events, but do not settle the form of the pending expansion.

Smallest supported repair: “Teamets beslut om att utöka försöket återstår”.

Draft: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar.”

Source: “I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

Obstruction: in Swedish, “nästa byggnad börjar” leaves the activity that starts unstated and readily evokes a building/construction starting, instead of the repair-log trial starting in that building. This is a source-syntax calque, not merely an alternative preferred synonym. The surrounding supplied account concerns the trial in buildings and preparation for its next site, not construction of a building; that context settles the implicit activity enough to render the speech idiomatically.

Smallest repair: “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan försöket börjar i nästa byggnad.” Preserve “Jag skulle”, the category-agreement time reference and the conditional stance. No changed natural-gender or number information results.

The other two translated quotations, and the first sentence of this quotation, retain meaning, stance, certainty and the speaker's practical voice. The preparation reservation survives. No additional translation findings.

# Case-study brief and source

SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.

## Brief

Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.

## Material

Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.

The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.

Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:

- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.

## Forbidden inferences / judging

No claim that software caused the shorter assignment time, saved money, delighted residents or rescued a helpless customer. Do not turn assignment time into completion time. The customer's reservation must survive. Judge whether quotations contribute experience beyond the surrounding narrative, whether supplier narration stays in third person and whether the suggested link accurately describes its destination.

Resolved language: sv (Swedish). Source quotation language: English. Target quotation language: Swedish.

## Claims

Every claim is supported by the text or its material, with exact attribution and proportionate strength. Preserve the state of knowledge: what is unknown or unclaimed is not thereby known not to have happened. Keep uncertainty where it exists and certainty where it is warranted. A fact, quotation, source, scene, personal experience or opinion attributed to somebody is never invented to complete a form. Name the actual source of an attributed claim rather than invoking unnamed studies or experts.

Circumstantial detail is a claim too: duration, manner, motive, absence and background all need support. So does an evaluative characterisation: calling a count high, low or modest needs a comparison, target, capacity or speaker assessment. Otherwise give the count with its exclusions, without that assessment.

A sequence or correlation establishes no cause. A causal verb such as *shortened* needs causal support; a causal hedge such as *suggests that it shortened* still adds that attribution. This boundary holds in the title, summary, headings and body alike. Preserve chronology, scope and qualifications wherever a claim appears.

A stated length constrains the use of material and is never a licence to add to it. When the material is insufficient, deliver the length the material supports and name what further material would close the gap. A supplied publication limit is binding; meeting it cannot justify invention or loss of a qualification that changes a claim.

# Quoting speech

Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.

Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.

When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.

## What may be repaired

The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

## What stays outside this

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.

## Swedish composition
Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not.

# Case-study brief and source

SYNTHETIC EVALUATION MATERIAL. This is the entire fictional source package. Source language: English. No external facts or quotations may be added.

## Brief

Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party. Approximately 400 words, as material allows. Markdown. No author name supplied. The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.

## Material

Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats. In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately. The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information. It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.

The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents. Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The trial lasted eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial. Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software. There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.

Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:

- “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
- “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
- “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures. The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs. The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism. All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided. Translation of the quotations is permitted, preserving stance and qualification.

## Forbidden inferences / judging

No claim that software caused the shorter assignment time, saved money, delighted residents or rescued a helpless customer. Do not turn assignment time into completion time. The customer's reservation must survive. Judge whether quotations contribute experience beyond the surrounding narrative, whether supplier narration stays in third person and whether the suggested link accurately describes its destination.
# Elm Quay samlar reparationsanmälningar i en gemensam vy

Av [ditt namn]

Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter. Tidigare förvarades telefonanmälningar och mejl separat. I september 2025 beslutade bolagets eget underhållsteam att prova en gemensam reparationslogg i två byggnader. Målet var att personal på olika skift skulle kunna se samma information.

## Elm Quay behöll telefonanmälningarna

Teamet valde Svale Systems efter att ha testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Underlaget innehåller ingen jämförelse med någon annan leverantör. De boende kunde fortsätta att anmäla reparationer per telefon, medan Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen.

Arbetsledaren för underhåll, Maya Lind, beskriver i en mejlintervju vad teamet ville åstadkomma:

– Vi ville att kvällsskiftet skulle kunna se vad morgonskiftet redan hade gjort. Kategorierna var våra; Svale hjälpte oss att lägga in dem i loggen.

## 31 reparationsanmälningar registrerades under försöket

Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, redovisar tiden från anmälan till tilldelning. Medianen var två arbetsdagar under försöket, jämfört med tre under den föregående åttaveckorsperioden. Anmälningar som gäller nödsituationer och arbeten beställda före försöket ingår inte i anteckningens underlag.

Perioderna hade olika arbetsbelastning. Anteckningen tillskriver uttryckligen inte programvaran skillnaden i tid. Det finns heller inga mätningar av kostnader, boendes nöjdhet eller tiden tills reparationerna var slutförda. Siffrorna ger därför inget besked om besparingar eller snabbare slutförda arbeten.

## Teamets beslut om att utöka försöket återstår

Försöket har ännu inte utökats. Teamet ska besluta efter att ha kontrollerat hur kategorierna fungerar för större reparationer. När Maya Lind ser tillbaka på förberedelserna beskriver arbetsledaren en erfarenhet inför nästa byggnad:

– Vi ägnade mer tid åt att enas om kategorierna än åt att lägga in de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan försöket börjar i nästa byggnad.

– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. Att ha en gemensam vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelser, säger Maya Lind om försöket.

## Läs checklistan inför genomförandet

Elm Quays erfarenhet visar vilka val och begränsningar ett försök kan behöva belysa. För dig som vill läsa vidare finns [Svales checklista för genomförandet](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).
Resolved language: sv (Swedish). Source quotation language: English. Target quotation language: Swedish.

## Claims

Every claim is supported by the text or its material, with exact attribution and proportionate strength. Preserve the state of knowledge: what is unknown or unclaimed is not thereby known not to have happened. Keep uncertainty where it exists and certainty where it is warranted. A fact, quotation, source, scene, personal experience or opinion attributed to somebody is never invented to complete a form. Name the actual source of an attributed claim rather than invoking unnamed studies or experts.

Circumstantial detail is a claim too: duration, manner, motive, absence and background all need support. So does an evaluative characterisation: calling a count high, low or modest needs a comparison, target, capacity or speaker assessment. Otherwise give the count with its exclusions, without that assessment.

A sequence or correlation establishes no cause. A causal verb such as *shortened* needs causal support; a causal hedge such as *suggests that it shortened* still adds that attribution. This boundary holds in the title, summary, headings and body alike. Preserve chronology, scope and qualifications wherever a claim appears.

A stated length constrains the use of material and is never a licence to add to it. When the material is insufficient, deliver the length the material supports and name what further material would close the gap. A supplied publication limit is binding; meeting it cannot justify invention or loss of a qualification that changes a claim.

# Quoting speech

Read this before putting quotation marks around anything somebody said. It applies to interview transcripts, recorded remarks, meeting notes, and any other material where the words are a person's rather than a document's.

Speech is not written prose, and a transcript quoted raw reads as carelessness towards the speaker rather than fidelity to them. So a spoken quotation may be repaired — cautiously, within a boundary that is easier to state than to feel your way to.

When translating permitted quotations, preserve meaning, stance, certainty and distinctive voice in idiomatic target-language speech, not source-language syntax. The restrictions below protect that substance; they do not require word-for-word translation. Make an implicit referent explicit only when the supplied context settles it. Where the meaning remains ambiguous, paraphrase what is established rather than inventing a fluent interpretation.

## What may be repaired

The syntax of speech: a sentence abandoned halfway and restarted, a subject left behind by its verb, a clause that never closes. Fillers — *you know*, *sort of*, *liksom*, *alltså* — where they carry nothing. Repetition that is the speaker searching for a word rather than insisting on one. False starts, and the small disfluencies a person does not hear themselves make.

That is the whole list. Everything on it is noise the speaker did not intend to produce, and removing it leaves what they meant to say.

## What may not

**Meaning.** Not narrowed, not widened, not sharpened. A speaker who said *most of them* has not said *all of them*, and one who said *we looked at it* has not said *we rejected it*.

**Stance.** Approval stays approval, reluctance stays reluctance, and a speaker who was careful not to blame anybody is not made to blame somebody by a tidier sentence.

**Certainty.** *I think*, *probably*, *as far as I know*, and *we are not sure yet* are the claim, not padding on it. Removing a hedge manufactures a confidence the speaker did not have; adding one takes away a confidence they did.

**Distinctive wording.** Where the speaker reached for an unusual word, an image, a piece of slang, or a phrasing that is theirs, it stays. Smoothing it into the register of the surrounding article is the most tempting of these failures and the one a reader can least detect.

**A self-correction.** Where a speaker gives a number or a fact and then corrects it, the correction is what they said. Quoting the first version is a misquotation; quoting a version that never existed — the correction with the correcting away — is worse.

**Anything additive.** Add no new meaning: no fact, stance, certainty, name, figure or connection that the speaker did not supply. A permitted repair or translation may change words only to render that same meaning.

## When to paraphrase instead

Where fidelity is uncertain, paraphrase. A paraphrase that attributes carefully — *she said the change had taken about a year, and that she was not sure it would hold* — is accurate, useful, and honest about what the material supports. A fluent direct quotation assembled out of a fragmentary answer is none of those things, however good it sounds.

The cases that should turn into paraphrase: material that is a summary of what somebody said rather than their words; a transcript too broken to repair inside the boundary above; several remarks that would have to be welded together to make one sentence; and any moment where you find yourself choosing between two readings of what the speaker meant.

Signal what the material actually is. Where the source is notes rather than a recording, the text says what the person said and does not pretend to their exact wording.

## What stays outside this

Whether the speaker approves the quotation. Quote approval is a human arrangement between the writer and the person quoted, and nothing here verifies it or stands in for it. A draft may say a quotation is unapproved; it may not treat the absence of approval as a problem it has solved.

## Swedish composition
Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not.
